_comment: WHAT THE STUDY RUNS. One file, because the scheme is implemented twice and the
two implementations have already drifted apart once without anything noticing
This file is READ BY TESTS ON BOTH SIDES, not just documented. rust/tests/
noise_gates.rs parses it and asserts the injector's own condition list and CLI
defaults agree with it; scripts/test_noise_conditions.py asserts every name here
resolves in noiseInject.CONDITIONS to the same parameters. A previous settings
file, scripts/noise_strategy_params.json, was never passed to the binary at all
and so silently meant nothing for the life of the project. This one fails a test
The names are the condition keys shared by both injectors.
Settled 2026-08-27 by the author, on the evidence in RERUN_PLAN.md section 13.9
and NOISE_DESIGN.md section 5.8: twelve replicates on real QM9, every condition
delivering the same amount of noise. Shape and contamination do not earn

stage_1_full_grid.name: gaussian
stage_1_full_grid.why: The reference case, and what both direct predecessors used, so the results stay comparable to theirs.

stage_1_full_grid.name: grouped_wider
stage_1_full_grid.why: Whole scaffold families get a larger error, still centred on the truth. Indistinguishable from Gaussian on its own -- it is here because it is the comparator that makes grouped_shifted interpretable. The pair is the claim; neither half is.

stage_1_full_grid.name: grouped_shifted
stage_1_full_grid.why: Whole scaffold families pushed in one direction. The ONLY zero-mean condition that separates: against grouped_wider at level 1.5 it costs 0.096 to 0.314 R2, at 2.5x to 7.4x the run-to-run spread, every p <= 0.003. Same amount of noise, same families, same targeting -- the only difference is direction.

stage_1_full_grid.name: censoring
stage_1_full_grid.why: Values past the assay limit recorded as the limit. The most prevalent real mechanism, not zero-mean, and it cannot be dose-matched, so it runs on its own axis (fraction of labels clipped).

stage_2_depth_only.name: student_t_nu5
stage_2_depth_only.why: One tail weight, not three. The three settings are within 0.006 R2 of each other and of Gaussian at the reporting level, against a test that could have seen 0.006 to 0.021. nu = 10 is nearly Gaussian by construction; nu = 3's per-run delivered dose has a 17% spread at level 1.5, which makes it the worst-behaved thing on the grid to report. nu = 5 is mid-ladder and well-behaved.

stage_2_depth_only.name: outlier_p10
stage_2_depth_only.why: One contamination fraction, not three. Same evidence: every step of the 1% -> 5% -> 10% ladder is under 0.005 R2. p = 10% is the top of Hampel's published range and the strongest contamination, so if anything is ever going to show, it shows there.

stage_2_depth_only.name: laplace
stage_2_depth_only.why: Kept, settled by the author 2026-08-27. Empirically indistinguishable from Gaussian on every model at both levels tested (largest 0.0087 R2 across roster models; the 0.0058 previously quoted here was a Ridge row, and Ridge is not in the study -- corrected 2026-08-27), so it buys a citation rather than a result -- but it is the only distribution family actually FITTED to real bioactivity error, and at 720 training runs (1.4% of the old design) the citation is cheap. Depth stage only; it is not in the full grid.

not_run.name: student_t_nu10
not_run.why: Within 0.0054 R2 of Gaussian at the reporting level (0.29 of the run-to-run spread, p = 0.24), and within 0.002 of nu = 5. Represented by student_t_nu5.

not_run.name: student_t_nu3
not_run.why: Within 0.0036 R2 of Gaussian at the reporting level, and within 0.006 of nu = 5. Represented by student_t_nu5.

not_run.name: outlier_p01
not_run.why: Within 0.0058 R2 of Gaussian at the reporting level. Represented by outlier_p10.

not_run.name: outlier_p05
not_run.why: Within 0.0034 R2 of Gaussian at the reporting level. Represented by outlier_p10. Note that outlier_p05 minus outlier_p01 reaches p = 0.001 on a difference of +0.003 R2 -- precision around zero, and the wrong sign for a dose response, not an effect.

not_run.name: skewed_draw
not_run.why: A centred Gamma draw, asymmetric by draw rather than by mechanism. Tested in scripts/setting_selection_test.py and NOT built into either injector. Nothing at the reporting level; -0.045 R2 for the random forest alone at level 1.5 and nothing for the other two models. The asymmetry story is carried by censoring and by grouped_shifted, both of which are mechanisms with sources behind them rather than a chosen distribution.

settings_that_follow._comment: The CLI defaults that make the single-setting decisions operative. Both injectors are tested against these.
